title: Ecology
description: The theme that closes the book, over four lessons and the third progress check: the six defined terms of the environment (ecology, the environment, global warming, a rain forest, wildlife, ozone depletion) and the extra definition that is really zoology, plus the words the theme works with (depletion, thinning, to endanger, extinct, fumes, to purify, to ban, deforestation, a drought, rainfall, consumption, to account for, to drill); the adverbs of degree, quite, very and too standing before the adjective while enough stands after it and before a noun, and the two structures that decide whether an action is still possible - enough to when the quality suffices and the action happens, too plus adjective plus to when it is excessive and the action cannot, and the negative case that catches everybody, where what fails is a quality that is missing rather than one in excess; four reports on the ozone layer, on warming, on the oceans and on the rain forests, every figure dated 1995, and the contradiction the book prints four pages apart between global warming being a fact and scientists being uncertain; four scrambled paragraphs on water scarcity whose order is fixed by their connectors alone, and the intruder that is not off-topic but off-argument, praising the benefits of irrigation in a text about a shortage and its causes; not only but also, the addition it expresses, the two elements of the same kind it joins and the agreement trap the book uses twice without teaching it, the verb agreeing with the second subject; the Tunisian anchor of the lesson, from the SONEDE to dams, mountain lakes and drilling; the simile compared with the metaphor and the personification, and the one-second test that separates them; and the four organisation tasks of the progress check - writing a topic sentence, inserting missing sentences, punctuating a paragraph and developing telegraphic notes
